original_card.question: Does one explicit extension of the connector alphabet offer a favorable completed budget?
methods: Construct and charge a legal extra operation on a minimal instance.
Prove a target-specific bound after adding one specified operation family.
original_card.acceptance_gate: State which fixed-alphabet premise changes and charge its implementation; do not declare it free. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Reproduce the 945-pairing control, then read Exact interface to list the allowed calls.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Add exactly one legally priced operation and test a tiny dirty-input instance before enumerating larger cases.
original_card.bottleneck_link: A new legal connector operation could change recursive interface cost; a larger census in the same alphabet is a separate side result.
allowed_variations: Choose one additional operation and a small source count for its first counterexample.
scope_change_triggers: Keeping the alphabet and only increasing the source count; record this as a changed assignment.
Extending a source-count census without naming a supplier/interface decision it could change; audit #2973 pruning concerns before relying on the affected predecessor exclusions.

actual_scope: All-n lower bound for restored F2 source-XOR words: L >= 2(n - c), so a connected restored word on n labels needs at least 2(n-1) calls, with attaining words for every n; plus the connector consequence X >= 2(2n-Q) under PR #2455's component inequality.
scope_change_reason: This keeps PR1340's paid source-XOR alphabet and removes the source-count restriction, which the card lists as a scope-change trigger. It answers Open next question 2 of ywz65's PR #2455, which asks for exactly this all-n theorem to settle the minimum-query source-XOR question left by PR #1898.
bottleneck_link: Side result: the source-restoration bill of the mutable-source connector becomes a closed-form floor at every source and query count, before any unequal-price tariff search. No supplier, alphabet extension or physical common-B access is established.
stop_rule: Stop at the first verified written theorem with attaining words and an exhaustive small-label corroboration. No tariff search or new connector construction.
evidence: PROOF.md proves L >= |T|+|S| for restored words (rank-one product lemma) and L >= 2(n-c) by induction removing a pure source or pure target. verify.py exhaustively joins every restored word for one to five labels (through lengths 2, 4, 6, 8 and 8), checks both inequalities on every restored directed arc set, confirms the first connected length 2(n-1), and checks star/path attaining words through twelve labels.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: What is the exact minimum length of a connected restored source-XOR word of odd length on n labels?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Odd restored words exist; their minimum decides which odd X counts can occur at the minimum query endpoint.
open_questions.first_step: The theorem gives at least 2n-1; the census attains it with length five on three labels and seven on four labels; five labels were joined only through length eight. Test whether 2n-1 is attained for every n >= 3.
open_questions.blocked_by: The proof bounds the length from below but constructs only even attaining words.

open_questions.question: Does the floor X >= 2(2n-Q) combine with the readout floors of PR #2677 to raise the 8- and 9-query tariff floors?
open_questions.why_it_matters: PR #2677 records only X >= 0 at eight and nine queries in its path-lowered class; X >= 4 and X >= 2 could raise those floors.
open_questions.first_step: Bind the n-source component inequality and PR #2677's readout floors to one shared model, then add the XOR term.
open_questions.blocked_by: The readout floors belong to a different schedule class; this package does not establish that they hold together with the XOR floor.
